title: Periodic Table and Properties - Chemistry - Atomic and Ionic Radii
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes the trend of atomic radius across a period (left to right) and its cause?
options: Increases due to additional electron shells
Decreases due to increasing effective nuclear charge ($Z_{eff}$)
Increases due to increased electron-electron repulsion
Decreases due to the lanthanoid contraction
questions.explain: Across a period, electrons are added to the same shell while protons are added to the nucleus. This increases the effective nuclear charge ($Z_{eff}$), pulling electrons closer and shrinking the radius.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Arrange the following species in order of increasing radius: $Mg^{2+}$, $Na^+$, $Ne$, $F^-$.
questions.explain: These species are **isoelectronic** (all have 10 electrons). The size is determined by the nuclear charge. $Mg$ has 12 protons, $Na$ 11, $Ne$ 10, $F​$ 9. Higher nuclear charge pulls the same number of electrons tighter. Thus, $Mg^{2+}$ is smallest and $F^-$ (with the fewest protons) is largest. (Note: $F^-$ is typically larger than $Ne$ due to lower Z).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Why is the radius of a cation always smaller than its neutral parent atom (e.g., $Na^+ < Na$)?
options: Loss of valence electrons increases effective nuclear charge per electron and may remove a shell
questions.explain: Removing an electron reduces electron-electron repulsion and, in many cases (like $Na \to Na^+$), removes the outermost shell entirely. The remaining electrons are held more tightly by the nucleus.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Identify the element with the largest atomic radius among the following:
questions.explain: Atomic radius increases down a group and decreases across a period. Potassium ($K​$) is in Period 4 (lower down than Li/F) and Group 1 (far left), making it the largest among these options.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following correctly compares the size of the chloride ion ($Cl^-$) and the chlorine atom ($Cl$)?
options: $Cl^- < Cl$ because the ion has fewer electrons
$Cl^- > Cl$ because the added electron increases repulsion
$Cl^- = Cl$ because the nucleus remains the same
$Cl^- < Cl$ because the effective nuclear charge increases
questions.explain: Anions are formed by gaining electrons. The added electron increases electron-electron repulsion in the valence shell, causing the electron cloud to expand, making the anion larger than the neutral atom.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: The atomic radii of Zirconium ($Zr$, Period 5) and Hafnium ($Hf$, Period 6) are almost identical (160 pm vs 159 pm). This anomaly is due to:
questions.explain: The filling of the 4f orbitals before Hafnium results in poor shielding of the nucleus. This causes a greater than expected attraction for the outer electrons, shrinking the radius of Period 6 transition metals to match Period 5. This is called the **Lanthanoid Contraction**.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In the isoelectronic series $S^{2-}, Cl^-, K^+, Ca^{2+}$, which ion has the largest radius?
questions.explain: In an isoelectronic series, size is inversely related to atomic number (Z). Sulfur ($Z=16$) has the fewest protons holding the 18 electrons, so $S^{2-}$ is the largest. Calcium ($Z=20$) has the most protons, making $Ca^{2+}$ the smallest.
